{{short description|Term in the mathematical theory of special functions}}
In the mathematical theory of [[special functions]], the '''Pochhammer ''k''-symbol''' and the '''''k''-gamma function''', introduced by Rafael Díaz and Eddy Pariguan <ref>
{{cite arXiv
 |date=2005
 |eprint=math/0405596
 |first=Rafael |last=Díaz
 |author2=Eddy Pariguan
 |title=On hypergeometric functions and k-Pochhammer symbol
 }}</ref> are generalizations of the [[Pochhammer symbol]] and [[gamma function]]. They differ from the Pochhammer symbol and gamma function in that they can be related to a general [[arithmetic progression]] in the same manner as those are related to the sequence of consecutive [[integer]]s.

==Definition==
The Pochhammer ''k''-symbol (''x'')<sub>''n,k''</sub> is defined as

: <math> 
\begin{align}
(x)_{n,k} & = x(x + k)(x + 2k) \cdots (x + (n-1)k)=\prod_{i=1}^n (x+(i-1)k) \\ 
          & = k^n \times \left(\frac{x}{k}\right)_n,\, 
\end{align} 
</math>

and the ''k''-gamma function Γ<sub>''k''</sub>, with ''k'' > 0, is defined as

: <math>\Gamma_k(x) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{n!k^n (nk)^{x/k - 1}}{(x)_{n,k}}. </math>

When ''k'' = 1 the standard Pochhammer symbol and gamma function are obtained.

Díaz and Pariguan use these definitions to demonstrate a number of properties of the [[hypergeometric function]]. Although Díaz and Pariguan restrict these symbols to ''k'' > 0, the Pochhammer ''k''-symbol as they define it is well-defined for all real ''k,'' and for negative ''k'' gives the [[falling factorial]], while for ''k'' = 0 it reduces to the [[Exponentiation|power]] ''x<sup>n</sup>''.

The Díaz and Pariguan paper does not address the many analogies between the Pochhammer ''k''-symbol and the power function, such as the fact that the [[binomial theorem]] can be extended to Pochhammer ''k''-symbols. It is true, however, that many equations involving the power function ''x<sup>n</sup>'' continue to hold when ''x<sup>n</sup>'' is replaced by (''x'')<sub>''n,k''</sub>.

== Continued Fractions, Congruences, and Finite Difference Equations ==

Jacobi-type [[generalized continued fraction|J-fractions]] for the ''ordinary'' [[generating function]] of the Pochhammer k-symbol, denoted in slightly different notation by <math>p_n(\alpha, R) := R(R+\alpha)\cdots(R+(n-1)\alpha)</math> for fixed <math>\alpha > 0</math> and some indeterminate parameter <math>R</math>, are considered in <ref>
{{citation 
 |date=2017
 |publisher=J. Integer Seq.
 |volume=20
 |url=https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL20/Schmidt/schmidt14.html
 |first=Maxie D. |last=Schmidt
 |title=Jacobi-Type Continued Fractions for the Ordinary Generating Functions of Generalized Factorial Functions
 |arxiv=1610.09691
 }}</ref> 
in the form of the next infinite [[continued fraction]] expansion given by

:<math>
\begin{align} 
\text{Conv}_h(\alpha, R; z) & := 
     \cfrac{1}{1 - R \cdot z - 
     \cfrac{\alpha R \cdot z^2}{ 
            1 - (R+2\alpha) \cdot z -
     \cfrac{2\alpha (R + \alpha) \cdot z^2}{ 
            1 - (R + 4\alpha) \cdot z - 
     \cfrac{3\alpha (R + 2\alpha) \cdot z^2}{ 
     \cdots}}}}.
\end{align} 
</math>

The rational <math>h^{th}</math> convergent function, <math>\text{Conv}_h(\alpha, R; z)</math>, to the full generating function for these products expanded by the last equation is given by

:<math>
\begin{align} 
\text{Conv}_h(\alpha, R; z) & := 
     \cfrac{1}{1 - R \cdot z - 
     \cfrac{\alpha R \cdot z^2}{ 
            1 - (R+2\alpha) \cdot z -
     \cfrac{2\alpha (R + \alpha) \cdot z^2}{ 
            1 - (R + 4\alpha) \cdot z - 
     \cfrac{3\alpha (R + 2\alpha) \cdot z^2}{ 
     \cfrac{\cdots}{1 - (R + 2 (h-1) \alpha) \cdot z}}}}} \\ 
     & = 
     \frac{\text{FP}_h(\alpha, R; z)}{\text{FQ}_h(\alpha, R; z)} = 
     \sum_{n=0}^{2h-1} p_n(\alpha, R) z^n + 
     \sum_{n=2h}^{\infty} \widetilde{e}_{h,n}(\alpha, R) z^n, 
\end{align} 
</math>

where the component convergent function sequences, <math>\text{FP}_h(\alpha, R; z)</math> and <math>\text{FQ}_h(\alpha, R; z)</math>, are given as closed-form sums in terms of the ordinary [[Pochhammer symbol]] and the [[Laguerre polynomials]] by

:<math>
\begin{align} 
\text{FP}_h(\alpha, R; z) & = \sum_{n=0}^{h-1}\left[\sum_{i=0}^n \binom{h}{i} (1-h-R/\alpha)_i (R/\alpha)_{n-i}\right] (\alpha z)^n \\ 
\text{FQ}_h(\alpha, R; z) & = \sum_{i=0}^h \binom{h}{i} (R/\alpha+h-i)_i(-\alpha z)^i \\ 
                          & = (-\alpha z)^h \cdot h! \cdot L_h^{(R/\alpha-1)}\left((\alpha z)^{-1}\right). 
\end{align} 
</math>

The rationality of the <math>h^{th}</math> convergent functions for all <math>h \geq 2</math>, combined with known enumerative properties of the J-fraction expansions, imply the following [[finite difference]] equations both exactly generating <math>(x)_{n,\alpha}</math> for all <math>n \geq 1</math>, and generating the symbol modulo <math>h \alpha^t</math> for some fixed integer <math>0 \leq t \leq h</math>:

:<math> 
\begin{align} 
(x)_{n,\alpha} & = \sum_{0 \leq k < n} \binom{n}{k+1} (-1)^k (x+(n-1)\alpha)_{k+1,-\alpha} (x)_{n-1-k,\alpha} \\ 
(x)_{n,\alpha} & \equiv \sum_{0 \leq k \leq n} \binom{h}{k} \alpha^{n+(t+1)k} (1-h-x/\alpha)_k (x/\alpha)_{n-k} && \pmod{h \alpha^t}. 
\end{align} 
</math>

The rationality of <math>\text{Conv}_h(\alpha, R; z)</math> also implies the next exact expansions of these products given by

:<math>(x)_{n,\alpha} = \sum_{j=1}^h c_{h,j}(\alpha, x) \times \ell_{h,j}(\alpha, x)^n, </math>

where the formula is expanded in terms of the special zeros of the [[Laguerre polynomials]], or equivalently, of the [[confluent hypergeometric function]], defined as the finite (ordered) set

:<math>\left(\ell_{h,j}(\alpha, x)\right)_{j=1}^h = \left\{ z_j : \alpha^h \times U\left(-h, \frac{x}{\alpha}, \frac{z}{\alpha}\right) = 0,\ 1 \leq j \leq h \right\}, </math>

and where <math>\text{Conv}_h(\alpha, R; z) := \sum_{j=1}^h c_{h,j}(\alpha, x) / (1-\ell_{h,j}(\alpha, x))</math> denotes the [[partial fraction decomposition]] of the rational <math>h^{th}</math> convergent function.

Additionally, since the denominator convergent functions, <math>\text{FQ}_h(\alpha, R; z)</math>, are expanded exactly through the [[Laguerre polynomials]] as above, we can exactly generate the Pochhammer k-symbol as the series coefficients

:<math>(x)_{n,\alpha} = \alpha^n \cdot [w^n]\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n+n_0-1} \binom{\frac{x}{\alpha}+i-1}{i} \times \frac{(-1/w)}{(i+1) L_i^{(x/\alpha-1)}(1/w) L_{i+1}^{(x/\alpha-1)}(1/w)}\right), </math>

for any prescribed integer <math>n_0 \geq 0</math>.

==Special Cases==

Special cases of the Pochhammer k-symbol, <math>(x)_{n,k}</math>, correspond to the following special cases of the [[falling and rising factorials]], including the [[Pochhammer symbol]], and the generalized cases of the multiple factorial functions ([[Double factorial#Generalizations|multifactorial]] functions), or the <math>\alpha</math>-factorial functions studied in the last two references by Schmidt:

* The Pochhammer symbol, or [[rising factorial]] function: <math>(x)_{n,1} \equiv (x)_n</math> 
* The [[falling factorial]] function: <math>(x)_{n,-1} \equiv x^{\underline{n}}</math> 
* The [[factorial|single factorial]] function: <math>n! = (1)_{n,1} = (n)_{n,-1}</math> 
* The [[double factorial]] function: <math>(2n-1)!! = (1)_{n,2} = (2n-1)_{n,-2}</math> 
* The multifactorial functions defined recursively by <math>n!_{(\alpha)} = n \cdot (n-\alpha)!_{(\alpha)}</math> for <math>\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{+}</math> and some offset <math>0 \leq d < \alpha</math>: <math>(\alpha n-d)!_{(\alpha)} = (\alpha-d)_{n,\alpha} = (\alpha n-d)_{n,-\alpha}</math> and <math>n!_{(\alpha)} = (n)_{\lfloor (n+\alpha-1) / \alpha \rfloor,-\alpha}</math>

The expansions of these ''k-symbol-related'' products considered termwise with respect to the coefficients of the powers of <math>x^k</math> (<math>1 \leq k \leq n</math>) for each finite <math>n \geq 1</math> are defined in the article on generalized [[Stirling numbers of the first kind]] and generalized [[Stirling polynomials#Stirling convolution polynomials|Stirling (convolution) polynomials]] in.<ref>
{{citation 
 |date=2010
 |publisher=J. Integer Seq.
 |volume=13
 |url=https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL13/Schmidt/multifact.html
 |first=Maxie D. |last=Schmidt
 |title=Generalized j-Factorial Functions, Polynomials, and Applications
 }}</ref>
